## COA Measurement Strategy — Multiple Myeloma Phase 3

The critical challenge for this proteasome inhibitor trial is capturing neuropathy burden alongside traditional MM symptom domains while ensuring regulatory acceptability through validated, multiplicity-controlled endpoints.

## Key Observations

• **Item library precedent exists**: TOURMALINE-MM1 used subscale approaches with EORTC QLQ-MY20 rather than full administration, reducing patient burden while achieving significant findings (p<0.05) [TI-001]. This creates regulatory precedent for calibrated PRO SOA approaches in MM proteasome inhibitor submissions.

• **PRO-CTCAE has strongest FDA endorsement**: FDA explicitly names PRO-CTCAE in the 2024 Core PRO Guidance as "an example of one acceptable item library for assessment of symptomatic adverse events" [IR-002]. This represents the most explicit FDA endorsement of any PRO instrument item library for oncology trials.

• **Neuropathy domain coverage is sparse**: Only 2 of 5 comparator trials measured peripheral neuropathy, with mixed results (BOSTON showed no significant change, PANORAMA 1 not reported) [TI-003, TI-005]. Given the known neuropathy risk profile of proteasome inhibitors, comprehensive coverage is essential for this mechanistic class.

• **EQ-5D is critical but inconsistently collected**: Only 2 of 5 comparator trials included utility measures, both showing significant improvement [TI-002, TI-004]. Without EQ-5D-5L, NICE cost-utility analysis becomes impossible and UK reimbursement is severely compromised.

• **Secondary endpoint positioning is standard**: In 21 KG trials for MM, 71% positioned PRO as secondary endpoints, 23% as exploratory, with no primary PRO endpoints documented. This evidence supports secondary positioning rather than exploratory designation for regulatory credibility.

• **Missing data and multiplicity control are leading rejection reasons**: REJ-039 (panobinostat) cited "excessive missing data" and "no alpha-control," while REJ-031 and REJ-032 cited "no multiplicity adjustment" [REJ-031, REJ-032, REJ-039]. Pre-specified hierarchical testing is essential for confirmatory status.

## HTA Requirements

| HTA Body | Required Instrument | In candidate list? | Action needed |
|----------|-------------------|-------------------|---------------|
| NICE | EQ-5D-5L | Yes | Include in final battery |
| ICER | EQ-5D-5L | Yes | Include in final battery |

## What the Expert Needs to Decide

1. **Whether to implement item library/calibrated SOA approach** for EORTC QLQ-MY20 to reduce burden from 50 to approximately 25-30 items per timepoint, following TOURMALINE-MM1 precedent.

2. **PRO-CTCAE domain selection** from the full item library to target proteasome inhibitor-specific AEs (neuropathy, fatigue, GI toxicities) while maintaining 15-20 item target.

3. **Hierarchical testing position** for PRO endpoints within the multiplicity structure, ensuring they follow primary efficacy endpoints (likely PFS) to enable confirmatory analysis.

4. **Assessment schedule alignment** with dosing cycles and expected time-to-benefit, considering that proteasome inhibitors typically show early symptomatic response within 2-3 cycles.

5. **Peripheral neuropathy measurement strategy** - whether to rely on PRO-CTCAE neuropathy items or add EORTC QLQ-CIPN20 for comprehensive coverage, given this is a class-specific concern.
